# Clipboard [Copy that carries notes, paste that recognizes them]

A cue's note is a slot value, so no selection can contain it — copy a cue on its
own and the text stays behind. `FootnoteClipboardExtension` fixes both
directions: copy carries the referenced notes, and paste turns footnote-bearing
HTML from other apps into real footnotes.

## Register the extension

```tsx twoslash
// @twoslash-cache: {"v":1,"hash":"9381a85be13f990f35d136af31eacf1c87623460ad56782854dae202e2e0cc9f","data":""}
// [!include ~/examples/clipboardExample.tsx:register]
```

Try it — the extension above, live:

<ClipboardExample />

## Copy

Copy appends the notes a selection references to both payloads: a GFM
footnote section in `text/html`, definition nodes in the Lexical JSON. The
walk is transitive — a carried note that cites further notes carries those
too.

## Paste

Paste routes every `text/html` payload through rule-based import, so
footnote-bearing HTML lands as real footnotes. Recognized sources:

- **Word** — desktop and web, including Safari's sanitized clipboard.
- **Google Docs** — exported or published HTML.
- **GitHub**'s rendered GFM, and this package's own `exportDOM`.

Source chrome — separators, literal `[1]` markers, backref arrows — is stripped
on the way in.

:::note
An in-editor copy from Google Docs doesn't carry its definitions (a Docs
limitation), so those cues paste with empty notes. Use Docs' exported or
published HTML to bring the notes across.
:::

## Re-keying on paste

An id is the join key between a cue and its note, so a paste must never let a
carried note clobber one already in the document. The rules:

- **Word and Docs footnotes** get fresh ids — their `1..n` numbering would
  otherwise collide with existing notes or an earlier paste.
- **A carried footnote whose id names a _different_ note here** is re-keyed on
  arrival, and its cues follow.
- **Same-content pastes keep their id** — so cutting a cue and pasting it back
  reconnects to its note, and multiple cues keep sharing one note.

:::note
Paste rerouting applies to _all_ `text/html` pastes for the editor, not only
footnote content — the extension owns the whole HTML paste path.
:::
